items.readable_text:
Content:
If the sides of a rectangle have fractional lengths, we find the rectangle's area by multiplying the fractions.

Content:
Look at the rectangle below. What is its area?

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/da449d706ab14cbbd94de68afd25e76d]

Content:
We find the area of the rectangle by multiplying the lengths of the sides:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{6}{5} \times \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{5 \times 5} = \dfrac{18}{25}]

Content:
So, the area of the rectangle is [MATH: \dfrac{18}{25}] square units.

First, we write [MATH: 2\,\dfrac{1}{2}] as an improper fraction:

[MATH: 2\,\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{(2\times 2)+1}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2}]

The area of the rectangle can be found by multiplying the lengths of the sides:

[MATH: \dfrac{4}{7} \times \dfrac{5}{2}]

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

[MATH: (4)/(7) × (5)/(2)|= (4)/(2) × (5)/(7); = 2 × (5)/(7); = (2 × 5)/(7); = (10)/([math]\color{blue}\,7\,[/math])]

So, the missing number is [MATH: 7.]

items.title: Finding the Area of a Rectangle

sections.normalized_html: The breadth of a rectangular park is [MATH: \dfrac 3 4\, \text{km}] and its length is [MATH: 1\, \dfrac 12 \, \text{km}.] Using the model below, find the area of the park, expressed as an improper fraction.
sections.readable_text:
The breadth of a rectangular park is [MATH: \dfrac 3 4\, \text{km}] and its length is [MATH: 1\, \dfrac 12 \, \text{km}.] Using the model below, find the area of the park, expressed as an improper fraction.

[IMG: /graphics/faf024f3123fd5a8ee39fdffc6ec365b]

sections.normalized_html:
To find the area, we need to multiply the lengths of the sides.

First we write [MATH: 1\,\dfrac{1}{2}] as an improper fraction:

[MATH: 1\,\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{(1\times2)+1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}]

Now, we find the area of the park by multiplying the lengths of its sides:

[MATH: \dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{3 \times 3}{4 \times 2} = \dfrac{9}{8}]

So, the area of the park is [MATH: \dfrac{9}{8}] square kilometers.
